The words

Away in a manger, no crib for a bed,
The little Lord Jesus laid down His sweet head;
The stars in the sky looked down where He lay,
The little Lord Jesus, asleep on the hay.

The cattle are lowing, the Baby awakes,
But little Lord Jesus, no crying He makes;
I love Thee, Lord Jesus, look down from the sky
And stay by my cradle till morning is nigh.

Be near me, Lord Jesus, I ask Thee to stay
Close by me for ever, and love me, I pray;
Bless all the dear children in Thy tender care,
And fit us for heaven, to live with Thee there.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum F and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s (C), on the first syllable of “Away”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 3/4 means three crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The first two verses of this children's carol were printed anonymously in Philadelphia in 1885; the third is usually credited to John Thomas McFarland. The tune MUELLER, by James Ramsey Murray, was published in 1887.

In Britain, and in many Nigerian churches, the same words are also sung to William J. Kirkpatrick's CRADLE SONG, with 'the stars in the bright sky' in the third line.

  • Verses 1 and 2, first printed in Philadelphia (1885): Anonymous
  • Verse 3: John Thomas McFarland (1851–1913)
  • Melody (1887): James Ramsey Murray (1841–1905)

Tune MUELLER by James Ramsey Murray (1841–1905); words by Anonymous and John Thomas McFarland (1851–1913).

Questions about Away in a Manger

What is the doh of Away in a Manger?

In this version, in F major, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does Away in a Manger start on?

It starts on s (C in F major), a pickup on the first syllable of “Away” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

Is Away in a Manger in the public domain?

Yes. John Thomas McFarland died in 1913, James Ramsey Murray died in 1905; the words were first published in 1885 and the music in 1887. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
